editorial:
Imagine a movie that feels more like a giant art show than a typical story. You are dropped into a wild world where Egyptian gods and old American car factories blend together. It follows a man moving through seven different lives, trying to figure out how to live forever. The vibe is very strange and slow, mixing opera music with weird sculptures and costume changes. It does not follow a normal plot, so you will feel like you are dreaming while you watch it.

What really sticks with you are the crazy visuals and the music, though the slow pace might make you restless if you want a fast story. It is not for everyone, but if you love art and odd ideas, you will find it fascinating. Since the images are so detailed, you should definitely try to find it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video or rent it on Apple TV to see every detail. If you are a collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is the way to go for the best quality.
endingExplained: In the final parts, the main character finishes his journey through the seven stages of rebirth. He moves past his human mistakes and ties his life back to the ancient Egyptian gods. The movie ends by showing that life and death are just a big loop. He finally finds a sense of peace and wholeness, blending his past lives into one final, artistic form that represents eternal life.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves experimental art and surreal stories.
